mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS increases > 0.25% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% over three months signals a weakening labor market, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where UNRATE increases > 0.5% over three months.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a contraction in consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenues and earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where RSAFS decreases > 1% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% year-over-year signals a strong supply-side expansion, which boosts corporate earnings and investor confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of instances where INDPRO increases > 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 jobs per month for three consecutive months signals a strong labor market, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of instances where PAYEMS increases > 200,000 jobs/month for 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% year-over-year signals a strong demand for housing, which boosts related industries and consumer confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of instances where HOUST increases > 10% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% month-over-month, it signals inflationary pressure coupled with tight monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: inflationary pressure with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP (GDPC1) grows by less than 1% quarter-over-quarter and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) increases by more than 0.3% in the same period, it signals a weakening economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth < 1% QoQ and UNRATE increases > 0.3% in the same period
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where GDPC1 growth < 1% QoQ and UNRATE increases > 0.3% in the same period.
